timeline_reviews.summary: Transport stream for the serial run; accounted in manifest but no semantic events projected from this source.
Serial parent trajectory: black-box probing, module and entry-file writes, edits, differential testing, fuzz replay, and final killed sweep.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized that the task was a black-box Python-to-Node port of furl/test6.py requiring ESM .mjs files in /output, manual argv handling, local modules only, and byte-aligned output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The main parallel plan launched a background workflow dedicated to probing dimensions, gap finding, follow-up probing, and synthesizing a spec. No child or parent step was assigned ownership of writing the JS implementation.
parallel.implementation: The parent ran extensive local probes and created helper scripts under /tmp or /workspace, but the trajectory contains no final implementation writes to /output/test6.mjs or /output/lib/*.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No implementation components were integrated or packaged. Artifact validation copied an empty file list even though the expected entry was test6.mjs.
parallel.verification: Verification consisted of probing the reference executable and checking workflow progress, not running a Node implementation against the reference or official-like tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with the workflow killed, unfinished probe children, no final response content, no deliverable files, and official evaluation at 0/163.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same ESM, manual argv, zero external dependency, and /output delivery obligations and treated the executable as the black-box oracle.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the whole lifecycle: probing behavior, deriving URL/argparse rules, writing modules and entry point, editing fixes, and running differential tests.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote lib/errors.mjs, lib/percent.mjs, lib/idna.mjs, lib/urlparse.mjs, lib/components.mjs, lib/netloc.mjs, lib/furl.mjs, lib/argparse.mjs, and test6.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The generated entry file imported the local modules, and artifact validation copied test6.mjs plus eight library modules from /output.
serial.verification: The serial run used corpus differential tests, argparse checks, ASCII sweeps, and randomized replay; it reached pass=146 fail=0 and pass=500 fail=0 before a later sweep was killed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also timed out and the final ASCII sweep exited 137; official evaluation still failed 35 of 163 cases, indicating ordinary remaining implementation gaps.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent saw the prompt requiring pure Node ESM, .mjs files, manual argv matching, local modules, /output placement, and black-box probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run saw the identical prompt and treated the executable as the oracle while satisfying the /output and .mjs file obligations in its artifact tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was similar, but serial carried the delivery requirements through to files while parallel stopped at probing/spec work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposition assigned dimension probers, gap critics, follow-up probers, and a spec synthesizer, but did not assign an implementation owner.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single-owner flow: explore behavior, state a model, write the library modules and entry file, then test and edit them.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed investigation without covering implementation ownership; serial maintained one owner across investigation, implementation, and validation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child context was organized as separate probe dimensions with structured findings and later spec synthesis, not as module interfaces or implementation contracts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor kept the behavioral model in one context and translated it directly into local module boundaries and imports.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context transfer was probe/report oriented and never created implementation interfaces; serial used accumulated findings directly in a coherent module design.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran many executable probes and helper sweeps but produced no final JavaScript implementation files under /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the support modules, edited them after differential failures, and wrote /output/test6.mjs as the executable entry point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete implementation path exists only in serial; parallel remained at empirical modeling and never materialized a runnable port.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The background workflow returned some probe results but the overall workflow state ended killed with result null and some probe children still in progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial local results were immediately used to update files and rerun tests, culminating in successful local differential runs before the final sweep was killed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel results did not mature into a usable implementation handoff; serial kept results inside the same owner loop and converted them into edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There was no integrated final tree: artifact validation saw an empty file list and no expected entry file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered an integrated /output tree containing test6.mjs and eight local library modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had a coherent submitted artifact tree while parallel had no final files to integrate or submit.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verification was black-box exploration of the source executable and did not verify a Node solution before closure; official evaluation scored 0/163.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local differential suites with 146/146 corpus passes and 500/500 randomized replay passes, though official evaluation still failed at 128/163.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had implementation-level verification evidence before closure; parallel only had oracle-probing evidence and no implementation to test.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full 2400 second run, used 17 workflow child logs, and timed out with no artifact files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but by closure it had written, edited, and locally tested a deliverable artifact tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both hit the time limit; serial spent enough of the budget on implementation and delivery, while parallel spent it on probing/spec work without implementation ownership.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail: parallel failed at 0/163 and serial failed at 128/163. The material task-solving difference is that serial produced and tested a real ESM artifact tree, while parallel never produced the required entry file or modules after delegating probe/spec work.
parallel_contributors: Probe/spec-only parallel workflow had no implementation owner for the required JS port.
Workflow ended killed and artifact validation copied an empty output tree.
serial_contributors: Single-owner serial flow converted probe findings into modules and test6.mjs.
Serial ran differential and randomized tests before timeout, leaving a partial but real solution.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial still missed hidden official cases despite local tests; those remaining semantic gaps are ordinary implementation incompleteness, not a parallel coordination label.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no pass/fail outcome difference; supported comparative contributors to artifact and score gap, not an exclusive root cause for all serial hidden failures

candidates.reason: The parallel plan delegated black-box probing and spec synthesis but assigned no active actor to write the required ESM implementation or entry file; closure copied no artifact files.
candidates.realized_consequence: No /output/test6.mjs or library files were delivered by the parallel run, leaving official evaluation at 0/163.
candidates.near_match_reason: The same episode involved heavy investigation, but the sharper boundary is that implementation was never owned rather than merely delayed after investigation.

candidates.reason: Rejected because no separately owned component implementations reached the point where interface reconciliation was the missing owned work; implementation itself was unowned.
Rejected because there were no completed implementation components or entry-point source waiting only for final packaging or placement.
Rejected because the observed failure was earlier than an end-to-end pipeline handoff; the plan lacked an implementation owner, not merely a stage-transition owner.
Rejected because no single mandatory preflight harness gate blocked otherwise-ready implementation; the delegated workflow was a broad probe/spec plan.
Rejected as the nearest suppressed chain: investigation dominated, but it never completed as a clean first phase followed by late implementation; no implementation owner was assigned.
Rejected because available capacity was not merely underallocated to an identified implementation path; the path had no explicit owner at all.
Rejected because child count, stalls, and timeout were downstream symptoms of the probe-only ownership plan, not an independent breadth/retry exhaustion episode.
Rejected because no single child owned an overbroad implementation task; children were scoped as probes or spec work and several completed probe reports.
Rejected because the child briefs were intentionally probe-specific and included their probe acceptance conditions; the missing item was not an omitted known requirement in an implementation brief.
Rejected because no independently owned components were delegated for later interoperability, so no absent interface contract produced incompatible components.
Rejected because there is no evidence that a known finding was lost in transfer and caused repeated work; the parent still had local probe outputs and status checks.
Rejected because returned probe reports were large but there is no distinct evidence that an available complete handoff could not be reduced; the decisive gap was no implementation ownership.
Rejected because no receiver acted on superseded workspace or requirement state; no stale transferred result is shown causing rework or invalid verification.
Rejected because no incompatible child reports or contracts remained unadjudicated at an integration point; no integration point was reached.
Rejected because the parent did not present or accept a whole-task completion; final.txt was empty and artifact validation later found no deliverable.
Rejected because workflow retry/stall entries do not show a replacement implementation attempt repeating prior work without inherited checkpoints; they were probe child retries in the same chain.

candidates.reason: Rejected because the observable stop is the overall timeout/workflow killed terminal state, not a parent decision to prematurely cancel a needed child before using a result.
Rejected because no complete candidate implementation or compatible component set existed ready for final placement before closure.
Rejected because no implementation change was merged after integrated verification; the parallel run never had an implementation merge.
Rejected because no delegated implementation was completed or retrievable; delegated work was probing and spec synthesis rather than implementation.
Rejected because the trapped or missing workflow result was not a verifier finding needed after an implementation; it was the unfinished probe/spec workflow.
Rejected because the workflow abort coincided with the terminal timeout and is downstream of the missing implementation owner, with no separate takeover window evidenced.
Rejected because the parent inspected some workflow progress and local findings; the issue was not one concrete available completed child result being ignored.
Rejected because the parent continued local probing and checked workflow/journal state instead of simply waiting blindly on available progress.
Rejected because concurrent agents did not write competing final implementation files or overlapping module designs requiring reconciliation.
Rejected because no two live agents edited the same source/config file in the final implementation workspace.
Rejected because no non-entry source file produced or owned by one live agent was replaced by another.
Rejected because no required executable or submitted entry point existed to overwrite.
Rejected because no broad cleanup or promotion replaced a current final output tree.
Rejected because probe scratch writes did not cause a concrete unstable final implementation state or provenance problem.
Rejected because no generated scratch artifact from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as stable input or as the reference environment.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel work split covered probing and spec synthesis but no active actor owned creating /output/test6.mjs and its local ESM modules; the run closed with no artifact files.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: No /output/test6.mjs or library files were delivered by the parallel run, leaving official evaluation at 0/163.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Investigation dominated the episode, but the stronger label is missing implementation ownership rather than a completed investigative phase that delayed an assigned implementation phase.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Serial Investigation, Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Critical-Path Starvation, Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, Blind Timeout Wait, and Late Finalization were treated as downstream or near-match descriptions of the same timeout/no-implementation chain.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the implementation ownership boundary cleared the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The retained set avoids splitting one probe-only workflow timeout chain into load, lifecycle, wait, takeover, and finalization labels.
